notes: The Nano Matter, Grove Relay Module, AC lightbulb, AC cable and wire nut are not in the catalogue, so they are new part types.
Only the three used Nano Matter pins (3V3, D4, GND) are given breadboard joins. The columns and rows are assumed, with the board straddling the centre gap. The photo doesn't show them exactly.
The photo shows the Grove relay connected through a Grove cable and a breadboard adapter. This is modelled as three jumper wires from breadboard holes to the relay's SIG, VCC and GND.
The tutorial says the relay is powered from 3V3 and controlled from D4. The ground wire is assumed.

Mains wiring is inferred from the photo and text. The AC cable's live conductor goes to relay COM, and relay NO goes to socket terminal 1 through a wire (wire4, as in the photo). The neutral conductor joins socket terminal 2 through a wire nut. Which socket terminal (1 or 2) goes to the relay is arbitrary because the socket's ports are symmetric. The cable's plug end is not modelled.
wire4 is a plain wire part (type jumper-wire) standing in for the mains-rated wire in the photo. It was added because the socket and relay terminals are both lugs and can't be joined directly.

The lightbulb-socket-e10 catalogue entry is already 'Bulb & Socket'. The separate AC bulb is kept because the parts list names it, and it is joined to the socket by a screw join with no port-level electrical edge.
The Google Nest Hub Max, the smartphone and the software are not part of the circuit, so they are omitted.
